                            STATEMENT OF REASONS FOR D ECISION
                          UNDER SECTION 40(5) OF THE ARCHIVES ACT 1983

        Series: A9755
        Control Symbol: 19
        Barcode: 3533548
        Title: Defence (RAAP) Unusual Aerial Sightings
        Decision Maker: Grant Battersby
        Designation: Access examiner APS6
        Date: 17 March 2015

        In accordance with requirements of subsection 8(1) of the Archives Act 1983 (Cth) (Archives
        Act), I am a person authorised by the Director-General, pursuant to an Instrument of
        Delegation, to make a decision in relation to access to the requested record.

        Basis for d ecision

        In making my decision, I considered:

           •   the content of the record requested
           •   the relevant provisions of the Archives Act 1983
           •   policy and guidelines of National Archives of Australia that relate to the access
               examination of Commonwealth records

        Decision

        After examining this record I have decided that this item is open with exceptions under
        33(1)(g) of the Archives Act for the reasons set out below.

        One folio (95) has been wholly exempted and 30 folios (66, 69, 71-72, 96-99, 106-108, 115-
        116, 118, 130-133, 144-145, 151-152, 156-159 and the file cover) have been partially
        exempted from public access.

        The material exempted contains information relating to the personal affairs of a person or
        persons and is the type of informatiorl that continues to be sensitive.

        Section 33(1)(g) of the Archives A ct 1983 provides that:

               a record is exempt if it contains information or matter the disclosure of which under
               this Act would involve the unreasonable disclosure of information relating to the
               personal affairs of any person (including a deceased person).




                                                       1



National Archives of Australia                                                           NAA: A9755, 19
                                                               NATIONAL
                                                               ARCH IVES
                            Australian Government


      The findings of facts

      This record contains:

         •    information concerning the personal affairs of a named person

      Reasons for decision

      The information exempted is of a nature such that its disclosure could lead to an
      unreasonable intrusion on the personal affairs of a person or persons.

      The information is of a kind that most members of the community would not want
      disclosed about themselves. There is nothing in the record that suggests the information
      was widely known in the community at the time.

      There is no evidence in the record that suggests that when the information was gathered,
      the subject expected it to be made publicly known or that it has become known in the
      intervening years.

      Disclosure of the information would involve the unreasonable disclosure of personal
      information.

      Review of decision

      The National Archives of Australia (the Archives) carefully examines records before
      deciding to exempt any part of them. As part of that process we may consult with other
      agencies which have expertise on specific national and international matters.

      If you do not agree with the decision, you can formally appeal within 28 days of receiving:

             1. by first applying to the Archives for an internal reconsideration of my decision;
                and

             2. if you still do not agree with the decision, yot1 can apply to the Adn1inistrative
                Appeals Tribunal for a review.

      For more information please read the National Archives Fact Sheet 12 What to do if we
      refuse yoit access (www.naa.gov.au /about-us/publications/fact-sheets/fsl2.aspx).

                      Dear


                               Thank you for making a telephone report of the unusual
                      aerial sighting experienced by yourself on 08 Oct 1989.
                      Preliminary investigations revealed that the phenomena noted by
                      yourself was possibly a high altitude, decaying orbit by the
                      COSMOS 1089 rocket motor stage; this assessment is supported by
                      the approximate time and duration of the sighting.

                               The present RAAF policy is that only those sightings
                      which suggest a Defence or security implication are further
                      investigated and a probable cause determined. However, there are a
                      number of civilian research organizations who also investigate
                      such phenomena, and who may be interested to hear of your
                      experience. The address of the Brisbane based organization
                      follows:

                                                UFO Research Queensland,
                                                PO Box 111,
                         •                      NORTH QUAY   QLD   4001


                      Yours faithfully,




                       H.      J . WAL.'l'r:l-{8

                 Mr G.BRAND,

                  Dear Mr Brand


                           Thank you for making a telephone report of the unusual
                  aerial sighting experienced by yourself on 10 July 1989.
                  Preliminary investigations suggested that the phenomena noted by
                  yourself was generated by atmospheric conditions.

                           The present RAAF policy is that only those sightings
                  which suggest a Defence or security implication are further
                  investigated and a probable cause determined. However, there are a
                  number of civilian research organizations who also investigate
                  such phenomena, and who may be interested to hear of your
                  experience. The address of the Brisbane based organization
                  follows:

                                                        UFO Research Queensland,
                                                        PO Box 111,
                                                        NORTH QUAY   QLD   4001

                                                                    '
                  Yours faithfully,

                      Mrs V. SWANSON,

                      CALLONVALE QLD 4116




                       Dear Mrs Swanson


                                Thank you for making a telephone report of the unusual
                       aerial sighting experienced by yourself on 10 July 1989.
                       Preliminary investigations suggested that the phenomena noted by
                       yourself was generated by atmospheric conditions.

                                The present RAAF policy is that only those sightings
                       which suggest a Defence or security implication are further
                       investigated and a probable cause determined. However, there are a
                       number of civilian research organizations who also investigate
                       such phenomena, and who may be interested to hear of your
                       experience. The address of the Brisbane based organization
                       follows:

                                                   UFO Research Queensland,
                                                   PO Box 111,
                                                   NORTH QUAY   QLD   4001


                       Yours faithfully,


                                                       ' .
                                               I




                       B. J. WALTERS
                       Squadron Leader
                       for Officer Commanding

                  Thank you for making a f elephone report of the unusual

         believed to pose a threat to our security.    Scheduled helicopter
         operations from Amberley on that date have been accounted for.

                  The present RAAF policy is that only those sightings
         which suggest a Defence or sec* rity implication are further

          Dear Mr Saunders,


                   Thank you for making a telephone report of the unusual
          aerial sighting experienced by yourself on 13 March 1989.
          Preliminary investigations revealed that the phenomena noted by
          yourself was Aurora Australis activity generated, in turn, by
          especially intensive sunspot activity around the period in
          question. This same activity also degraded both high-frequency
          and satellite communications around Australia at the same time.

                   The present RAAF policy is that only those sightings
          which suggest a Defence or security implication are further
          investigated and a probable cause determined. However, there are a .
          number of civilian research organizations who also investigate
          such phenomena, and who may be interested to hear of your
          experience. The address of the Brisbane based organization
          follows:

                     UFO Research Queensland,
                     PO Box 111,
                     NORTH QUAY   QLD   4001


          Yours faithfully,




          B. J. WALTERS
          Squadron Leader
          for Officer Commanding

                                                                  21 December 1988
                              82WG 5/113/AIR Pt 1 (19)
     IN RE PLY QUOTE...........   .




                Mr N.Palmer
                16 Edgar st
                Eastern Heights              QLD 4305

                Dear Mr Palm.er
                          Thank you for making a telephone report of the unusual
                aerial sighting experienced by yourself on 11 December 1988.
                Preliminary investigations have revealed a probable cause for
                the sighting; it is not believed to pose a threat to our security .

                          No local military air traffic was active at the
                time. Preliminary investigations have shown correlation between
                your sighting and at least two Regular Public Transport CRPT>
                airline movements into Brisbane in that time frame. The distortion
                effect of the atmosphere on reflections of aircraft navigation
                lighting during thunderstorm activity is a well known phenomenon,
                and probably accounts for your sighting.

                          The present RAAF policy is that only those sightings
                which suggest a Defence or security implication are further
                investigated and a probable cause determined. However, there are a
                number of civilian research organizations who also investigate
                such phenomena, and who may be interested to hear of your
                experience. The address of the Brisbane based organisation
                follows:

                                      UFO Research Queensland,
                                      PO Box 111
                                      NORTH QUAY QLD 4001


                Yours faithfully,




                (B.J.WALTERS)
                SQUADRON LEADER
                for Officer Commanding

                    Dear Mr


                             Thank you for making a telephone report of the unusual
                    aerial sighting experienced by yourself, and reported by yourself.
                    Both Preliminary Investigations and Air Traffic Control advice
                    indicate that you probably observed night air-to-air combat
                    exercises involving F/A-18 <HORNET) aircraft operating in
                  ' Restricted Area R674, just abeam coastal Brisbane. The high
                    crossing rates of the aircraft involved , as reflected by the
                    apparent tracks of their navigation/anti-collision lights, would
                    generate a similar phenomenon to that reported by you.
                             For information, the present RAAF policy is that only
                    those sightings which suggest a Defence or security implication
                    are further investigated. There are a number of civilian research
                    organisations who also investigate such phenomena, and the address
                    of the Brisbane based organisations follows:
                                                 UFO Research Queensland,
                                                 PO Box 111,
                                                 NOR'rH QUAY  QLD  4001


                    Yours faithfully,




                    B. J. WALTERS
                    Squadron Leader
                    for Officer Commanding

      LOGANVILLAGE QLD      4129

      Dear Mrs. Mclean,

                Thank you for making a telephone report of the unusual aerial sighting
      experienced by yourself on 10 September 1988. Unfortunately, preliminary
      investigations have so far failed to reveal a probable cause for the sighting,
      although it is not believed to pose a threat to our security. Your particular
      sighting, as reported, could have been of localized night helicopter operations.
                The present RAAF policy is that only those sightings which suggest a
      Defence or security implication are further investigated and a probable cause
      detennined. However, there are a number of civilian research organisations who
      also investigate such phenomena, and who may be interested to hear of your
      experience. The address of the Brisbane based organisation follows:
                UFO Research Queensland,
                PO Box 111,
                NORTH QUAY QLD 4001

      Yours faithfully,




      B.J. WALTERS
      Squadron Leader
      for Officer Comnanding

                                              The investigation of reports of U.F.O.s in Australia is
                                  carried out by the Roya.1 A.Ustralian Air Force , Directorate of Air
                                  Force Intelligen~e, at the Department of Air in Canberra~       A
                                  considerable amount of effor t is spent !n investigating each report
                                  ancl the majority of observer$ are intervievred by selected RJ..A.F • . •
                                  personnel .

                                            Between 23rd January 1960 and 30th December 1971, the RAAF
                                  received 595 U. F, Or reports , Pepartment of Air has assessed that
                                  93 percent were explainable by present scientific knowledge .   Six
                                  percent of the reports did not provide sufficient information to
                                  permit proper analysis_ and evaluatio                    the reports


                '       (;,   (
                                               The United Kingdom Air Ministry has stated that on an
                                  averaurre , 90 percent of the sightings it investigates are explainable
                                  by causes ranging from meteorological ball, ons and meteors to aircraft
                                  lights .     The other 10 percent probably remain unexplained because of
                                  lack of reliable information.

                         -1.                   In 1966 the University of Colorado , under contract to the
                                  U. S. A. F., spent t\-;o years processing and investigating all American
                                  reports .     Its findings have been published by Bantam Books as the
                                   ' Condon Report '.     Its general conclusion is that 'nothing has come
                                  from the study of U. F. O. s in the past 21 years that has added to
                                  scientific knowledge' and that 'furt?er extensive study of U. F. O. s
                                  probably cannot be justified in the expectation that science wi ll be
.
,;
                                  advc.:.nccd thereby '.    A panel of eminent scientists , chosen by the U. S•
                                  National Academy of Sciences, has examined and endorsed the Condon
                                  Report •
                    •
                          8.                   The U. S.A. F. 'Project Blue Book ' investigation of
                                  unidentifiGd aerial object:5ss between 1953 and 1~65 analysed 7 , 641
                                  U. F. O. r eports.    It concludod that :

                                            a.    80 percent of sightings \7ere natural phenomena,
                                                  hoaxes, birds or man- made objects ;

                                            b•    17 percent of sightings provided insufficient
                                                  data to permit thorough analysis and evaluatiun; and

                                             c~   three per cent were unidentified,
